07-155.r: Budget 2016-17 → 15% surcharge on individual income above Rs. 1 crore.

07-156.r: Budget 2011-12 created 'Very Senior Citizen' category → 80 years and above; Senior Citizen = 60 to below 80 years.

07-157.r: Budget 2005-06 → senior citizens exempt from income tax up to Rs. 1.50 lakh; now (old regime) Rs. 3.00 lakh senior, Rs. 5.00 lakh very senior.

07-158.r: Central Sales Tax → levied on inter-state trade and in Union Territories; SEZs exempt; now subsumed in GST (July 1, 2017).

07-159.r: Highest growth in Centre's Gross Tax Revenue (2013-14 to 2016-17) → 2016-17 (17.9%); 2015-16 was 16.9%.

07-160.r: Two largest Central tax sources at question time → Union excise and customs duties (option c); now Income Tax (19%), GST (18%), Corporation Tax (17%).

07-161.r: Customs plus excise share of Centre's revenue receipts in 1995-96 (B.E.) → 45.01%; in 2024-25 interim customs 7.7%, excise 10.6%.
07-161.c: Book gives no single answer: customs and excise made up 45.01% of the Centre's revenue receipts in 1995-96 (B.E.), above every option.

07-162.r: Gross tax revenue order at question time: Corporation Tax > Income Tax > Union Excise > Service Tax (option c); now Income Tax > GST > Corporation Tax.

07-163.r: Budget 2020-21 share of receipts: Corporation Tax 18%, Income Tax 17%, Customs 4%, Central Excise 7%.

07-164.r: Order at question time: corporation tax > other income tax > customs > Union excise (option b); 2024-25: taxes on income 30.18%, GST 27.87%, corporation tax 27.22%.

07-165.r: Most important Union tax source in 2009-10 → Corporation Tax.

07-166.r: Largest Union tax source 2013-14 → Corporation Tax; 2024-25 interim: Income Tax Rs. 1156000 crore, GST Rs. 1067650 crore, Corporation Tax Rs. 1042830 crore.

07-167.r: Largest tax revenue source now → Income Tax (then GST, Corporation Tax); in 2004-05 and 2005-06 Union excise duties were largest.
07-167.c: By the book's own note, Union excise (option c) was right at question time; answer (a) reflects present data.

07-168.r: Maximum tax revenue to Centre in 2007-08 → Corporation Tax; now Income Tax 19%, GST 18%, Corporation Tax 17% of receipts.

07-169.r: Largest tax source in Union Budget 2005-06 → Union excise duties, ahead of corporation tax (the book wrongly prints corporation tax).
07-169.c: Book's (a) is wrong for 2005-06: in that Budget, Union excise (c) was the largest source, ahead of corporation tax, as the book's own note on the previous question says.

07-170.r: Union excise share of gross tax revenue fell sharply: 30.4% (2005-06) → 16.5% (2009-10); now about 8.32%.

07-171.r: Road tax → levied by State governments, not the Union; service tax, education cess and customs duty are Union levies.

07-172.r: Stamp duties (in Union List) → levied by Union, collected and appropriated by States.

07-173.r: After the Eightieth Amendment (2000), net proceeds of all Union taxes (minus cess, surcharge, collection cost) form the divisible pool shared with States.
07-173.c: Book gives no single answer: since the Eightieth Amendment (2000) all Union taxes except cesses and surcharges are shared with States, so both (a) and (b) fit.

07-174.r: Income tax → levied and collected by the Union; net proceeds shared between Union and States as per Finance Commission.

07-175.r: Union-only sources (Union List) → customs duties and corporation tax (proceeds now shared via Finance Commission); sales tax, land revenue, holding tax are State sources.

07-176.r: Not a direct tax → sales tax (burden can be shifted); income tax, wealth tax and estate duty are direct (impact and incidence on same person).

07-177.r: At question time (2004-06) Union excise was Centre's highest tax source (option c); now Income Tax, GST, Corporation Tax; income tax is direct, customs indirect.

07-178.r: Capital Gain Tax → sale of property; Central Excise Duty → factory produce; Customs Duty → imports; Corporate tax → company income.

07-180.r: Corporation tax → levied and collected by the Union and now shared with States via Finance Commission; at question time it belonged to the Union exclusively.
07-180.c: Book says (d) was right at question time; answer (c) reflects present practice.

07-181.r: Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) → first in Budget 1987-88, withdrawn 1990, reintroduced in Budget 1996-97 (from 1 April 1997) to tax 'zero tax companies'.

07-182.r: MODVAT (Modified Value Added Tax, 1986) → excise duty, to reduce tax cascading; CENVAT also relates to Union excise duties.

07-185.r: VAT features: tax on value added at each stage, multi-point destination based, borne by final consumer; it is not mainly a Central subject.

07-187.r: VAT → introduced April 01, 2005 (L.K. Jha Committee, 1978); Haryana first (April 2003); Uttar Pradesh last (2008); Chhattisgarh and UP initially stayed out.

07-191.r: Sales tax not levied (question period) → Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep; GST applies across India since 1 July 2017.

07-192.r: Wealth tax → Wealth Tax Act 1957; abolished in Budget 2015-16, replaced by a surcharge on high-income individuals, HUFs and companies.

07-193.r: Service tax → introduced 1 July 1994 on the recommendation of Raja J. Chelliah Committee on Tax Reforms.

07-194.r: Service tax → indirect tax, introduced 1994-95 (Chelliah Committee); replaced by GST from 1 July 2017.

07-196.r: Service tax: 10% → 12% (Budget 2006-07) → 14% (Budget 2015-16); plus 0.5% clean India and 0.5% agriculture welfare cess in 2016-17.

07-197.r: Service tax rate at question time (2006) → 12% (option b); later raised to 14%.

07-198.r: Services under service tax in 2009-10 → 109 (nearest option 110); 117 in 2010-11, 119 in 2011-12; negative list from 2012-13.

07-199.r: Income tax introduced in India → James Wilson, 1860 (first Income Tax Act; income in four schedules).
07-199.c: Explanation's assent date '24 July, 1960' should read 1860.

07-200.r: Income tax does not directly raise commodity prices; trade tax, import duty and excise duty do (they are indirect taxes).
07-200.c: Book's explanation calls trade tax, import duty and excise 'direct taxes'; they are indirect.

07-201.r: Tax on imports and exports → customs duty (levied by the Union).

07-202.r: Direct tax → income tax (burden cannot be shifted); excise duty, octroi and sales tax are indirect.

07-203.r: Excise duty → indirect tax levied on production, sale or licence of certain goods.

07-204.r: Direct taxes (cannot be shifted): income, corporation, wealth, property, gift tax; indirect (shifted): customs, excise, service tax, sales tax, GST, VAT.

07-208.r: Fringe Benefit Tax (2005, abolished 2009), Interest Tax (1974 Act) and Securities Transaction Tax (1 October 2004) → all taken as direct taxes.
07-208.c: The explanation calls Interest Tax 'indirect', but it was a tax on lenders' interest income under the 1974 Act, run by income-tax authorities; (d) rightly treats it as direct.

07-209.r: Sales tax on toothpaste (pre-GST) → imposed and collected by the State Government; Central Sales Tax applied to inter-state sales.

07-210.r: Capital Gains Tax → on profit from sale of capital assets, not corporate income; FBT, MAT and tax on company profit relate to corporate income.

07-211.r: Entertainment tax → State List (List-II, Seventh Schedule), not levied by the Union; gift tax, personal income tax and corporation tax are Union taxes.

07-212.r: Corporation tax → levied by the Union, not States; entertainment tax, State excise duty and agricultural income tax are State taxes.

07-213.r: Customs duty → Central tax on imports and exports, not State tax revenue; land revenue, registration fee and commercial tax are State taxes.

07-214.r: Excise duty on liquor → imposed by State Governments (State List, Seventh Schedule).

07-215.r: Commodity Transaction Tax → introduced in Union Budget 2013-14; 0.01% on non-agricultural commodity futures.

07-216.r: Telecom Adjusted Gross Revenue (DoT view, upheld by SC October 2019) includes interest, dividend and forex gains; non-telecom revenue excluded from 15 September 2021.

07-217.r: e-Sahyog → Income Tax Department, launched 27 October 2015 to resolve return mismatches online.

07-218.r: Gratuity ceiling (Payment of Gratuity Act 1972, 10 or more employees) → Rs. 10 lakh at question time (option c); Rs. 25 lakh from 1 January 2024.

07-219.r: Voluntary Disclosure of Income Scheme 1997 → ran from 1 July 1997 to 31 December 1997.

07-220.r: Income Declaration Scheme 2016 → about Rs. 65,250 crore black money declared till September 30, 2016 (announced by Arun Jaitley, October 1, 2016).

07-221.r: Finance Commission (Article 280, every fifth year) → recommends sharing of Union tax proceeds and grants between Union and States.

07-225.r: Non-plan grants to States → on Finance Commission recommendations (Article 280(3)(b): principles of grants-in-aid from Consolidated Fund).

07-226.r: Wrong: 'recommendations of Planning and Finance Commissions are binding'; both are recommendatory. FC → non-plan resources; PC → plan resources.

07-227.r: Agricultural income tax → State tax, not shared under Finance Commission award; all Union taxes are shareable after the Eightieth Amendment (2000).

07-228.r: 15th Finance Commission (27 November 2017): Chairman N.K. Singh; members Ajay Narayan Jha, Anoop Singh, Ashok Lahiri, Ramesh Chand (part-time); Sudipto Mundle not a member.

07-229.r: 15th FC (N.K. Singh, November 27, 2017): first report for 2020-21 (December 5, 2019); final report for 2021-26 (November 9, 2020), not 2020-25.
07-229.t: 16th FC: Arvind Panagariya, constituted 31 December 2023; award period from 1 April 2026.

07-230.r: Bihar's share in divisible pool (15th FC) → 10.061% (2020-21), 10.058% (2021-26), second after UP (17.931%); was 9.67% under 14th FC.

07-232.r: 15th FC horizontal devolution: population 15.0%, area 15.0%, income distance 45.0%, forest and ecology 10.0%, demographic performance 12.5%, tax and fiscal effort 2.5%.
07-232.t: Governance reforms and stable government are not criteria.

07-233.r: 14th Finance Commission raised States' share of Union taxes from 32% to 42%; 15th FC → 41% (1% for new UTs of J&K and Ladakh).

07-234.r: 14th Finance Commission (Dr. Y.V. Reddy, appointed 2 January 2013) → States' share raised from 32% to 42%; no sector-specific grants.

07-237.r: 13th Finance Commission → Dr. Vijay L. Kelkar (November 2007); award period 2010-15, from 1 April 2010.

07-239.r: 13th Finance Commission → States' share 32% of net proceeds of Central taxes (12th FC: 30.5%).

07-241.r: Thirteenth Finance Commission → combined Centre and States debt-GDP target 68% by 2014-15; also a road map for fiscal and revenue deficits.

07-242.r: 13th FC devolution: highest weight → fiscal capacity distance 47.5% (population 1971 25.0%, fiscal discipline 17.5%, area 10.0%).

07-243.r: 13th FC: GST design with a compensation package tied to adherence; specified share of central taxes to local bodies as grants; no job-creation design.

07-244.r: Finance Commission chairmen: 1st K.C. Neogy (1951); 9th N.K.P. Salve; 10th K.C. Pant; 11th A.M. Khusro; 12th C. Rangarajan; Thirteenth Kelkar; Fourteenth Y.V. Reddy; 15th N.K. Singh.

07-248.r: 12th Finance Commission (Dr. C. Rangarajan, 1st November 2002) → States' share 30.5% of net Union taxes (11th FC: 29.5%).

07-249.r: Twelfth Finance Commission → revenue deficit of Centre and States to be zero by 2009-10 (not achieved: 0.7% of GDP in 2009-10 RE).

07-250.r: 11th Finance Commission → States' share 29.5% of shareable Central taxes (28% for States levying sales tax on sugar, tobacco, man-made textiles).

07-251.r: Tenth Finance Commission → single divisible pool; States' share 29% of all shareable central taxes (15th FC: 41%).

07-252.r: Committees: Disinvestment → C. Rangarajan (1992); Industrial sickness → Onkar Goswami (1993); Tax reforms → Raja Chelliah (1991); Insurance reforms → R.N. Malhotra (1993).
